## AI-Generated Fix (php)

```php
<?php

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::get('/.env', function () {
    abort(404);
});

// Alternatively, ensure the web server configuration blocks access to .env files.
// For Apache, add the following to your .htaccess file:
//
// <Files ".env">
//     Order allow,deny
//     Deny from all
// </Files>

// For Nginx, add the following to your server block:
//
// location ~* \.env {
//     deny all;
// }

```

---

## Explanation

The vulnerability was due to the .env file being publicly accessible, which can expose sensitive information. The fix involves creating a route in Laravel that returns a 404 error when attempting to access the .env file, effectively hiding it from public access. Additionally, web server configurations for Apache and Nginx are provided to block access at the server level, ensuring the file remains secure.
